solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knock off article covering one case of vice

indicators.note: the article is wrapped around the numeral, so one piece covers the other

parts.note: the definite article is 'the'
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thief nicks an item that holds one example of some wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock off' looks like it means imitate or stop work, but here it is slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off is informal slang for stealing something, the same act as to steal.

clue.text: Advantageous situation for European with attitude

parts.note: a Pole is a European, a native of Poland
an attitude is a position or stance on something

explanation.surface: A good spot for a European who has strong opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole position is the front place on the starting grid in motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The front slot on a race's starting grid gives the best start, so the phrase means any favourable place.

clue.text: What ruminants need is perhaps a spare gut

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Cud-chewing animals seem to need an extra stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on ruminants having several stomachs; 'perhaps' rearranges A SPARE GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grazing land, which cattle and sheep need for food.

clue.text: Left a box on first-class return from country

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV

indicators.note: return means the first-class symbol is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a crate when coming home from abroad in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping register's top grade, so it means first-class; 'box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state, one of the nations of northern Europe.

clue.text: Doctor too repellent, huh? I don't believe you!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A patient finds a physician far too off-putting and sceptically grunts disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, not a medic: it rearranges TOO REPELLENT HUH.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is a British retort meaning the speaker thinks they are being teased or lied to.

clue.text: Locks after Schubert's opening strains

indicators.note: the locks come after the first letter in the answer
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: Lengths of hair follow the first bars of a Schubert piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Strains looks musical alongside Schubert, but it means tensions or pressures.
explanation.definitionFit: Stresses and strains are both pressures or tensions put on something.

clue.text: Compare notes on the way back, revealing application

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
revealing means showing what lies within the words, here a run of letters across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two people swap observations on the return trip, which proves illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'revealing application' as the definition, leaving the hidden step with no indicator; 'revealing' is that indicator, and 'application' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A toner is a cosmetic lotion, something applied to the skin.

clue.text: Has an obligation to accommodate Vera's cows

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: someone who has an obligation owes something
the name Vera, its possessive adding no letters

explanation.surface: A farmer is bound to find room for Vera's cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cows' is a verb meaning intimidates, not the farm animals the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, as to overawe is to subdue with awe.

clue.text: TV doctor given a directive to stop,

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time traveller of the long-running BBC series

explanation.surface: A television physician receives an order to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a BBC science-fiction drama; 'given' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a call telling a horse, or a person, to halt.

clue.text: Sources of noise from wildcats crossing a river

indicators.note: the wildcats go across the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: lynxes are wildcats

explanation.surface: Big cats wade across a river making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts AR inside LYNXES.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat produces sound, so it is a source of noise.

clue.text: Save lift for transport from gala

indicators.note: transport carries something away, moving the letters into new places

explanation.surface: Keep the elevator to carry people away from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transport' rearranges SAVE LIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special occasion, much like a fete.

clue.text: Porterhouse perhaps admitting right run of luck?

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the right goes inside

parts.note: porterhouse is a cut of beef, an example of a steak

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a fine cut of beef brings good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags porterhouse as an example of a steak; 'admitting' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning or losing streak is an unbroken series of good or bad luck.

clue.text: Rebukes salesman, as chore goes wrong

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: something that goes wrong is upset, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A boss scolds a salesman because a task fails.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep is a travelling sales representative, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebukes and reproaches are both expressions of disapproval, here as verbs.

clue.text: Teetotallers finally interrupting consumer's celebration

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a consumer of food is an eater

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Non-drinkers break into a shopper's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives S from Teetotallers, and 'interrupting' puts it inside EATER; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the resurrection is a celebration held in spring.

clue.text: Kept apart, even in sitting

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: sitting means seated
par means even or equal, as in on a par

explanation.surface: Children were split up even though seated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' tempts as an alternate-letters signal, but it means equal, as in 'on a par'.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated means kept apart from one another, divided.

clue.text: Flower we harvested for beastly character

indicators.note: harvested crops are gathered and churned up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: We picked a bloom for an unpleasant person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harvested' rearranges FLOWER WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who becomes a wolf at full moon is a monstrous creature of folklore.

clue.text: Peaks are mainly pasture

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to pasture animals is to graze or browse

explanation.surface: Mountain tops are largely grazing land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasture' is a verb meaning graze, BROWSE, and 'mainly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow of a hill is its top, so brows are summits.

clue.text: Change bed again, causing some banter

indicators.note: change says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Making the bed twice leads to some joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges BED AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty conversation, light teasing talk.

clue.text: A spent force in Spain?

parts.note: a former currency that can no longer be spent, replaced by the euro, so a spent force in a second sense

explanation.surface: A Spanish power has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Spent force usually means something past its best; here it is money once spent in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of Spain, replaced in 2002, is literally finished as spending money.

clue.text: Lacking water, they add red to brew

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Thirsty people add red wine to their beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to brew' rearranges THEY ADD RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dried out has lost or lacks its water.

clue.text: Cape benefactor finishes early, crossing motorway

indicators.note: crossing means the shortened word spans the motorway, wrapping it
something that finishes early stops before its last letter

parts.note: a donor is a benefactor
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A generous giver leaves early to cross the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main London-to-Leeds motorway, written with I for the digit; a domino is the masquerade cloak, not the game tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn at masquerades, a kind of cape.

clue.text: Result in English and Latin is poor

indicators.note: poor work is badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pupil's English and Latin grades are poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result in' is a verb phrase, matching the verb in the answer, not the noun result.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve or bring it about as a consequence.

clue.text: Language used to reject writer with a brief lie

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the writer is turned around

parts.note: a pen is a writer

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing a final letter

explanation.surface: Speech is used to rebuff an author with a short fib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' is the definition at the front; 'used' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali is the national tongue of Nepal, spoken across the Himalayan nation.

clue.text: Accept trouble with physical training

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Agree to some hassle along with exercise classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or a plan is to accept and take it up.

clue.text: Things left for new workers after cutting remark by fifty per cent?

indicators.note: the new workers come after the shortened word
cutting by fifty per cent keeps only half of the word, its first half

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: New staff arrive once a comment has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting ... by fifty per cent' halves REMARK to REM.
explanation.definitionFit: Remnants are the leftover pieces, what remains after the rest is gone.

clue.text: State to go red in America anticipates a party

indicators.note: anticipates means comes before, so this piece leads

parts.note: to colour is to blush, spelt the American way
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An American blushes ahead of a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Colour as a verb means blush; American spelling drops the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty United States, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Hope to finish before eleven — time to leave

indicators.note: before means this letter comes first in the answer
to finish picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A football team hopes to end ahead with time running out.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven also suggests a football team, but here it is the Roman XI.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, so it means to leave.

clue.text: Cancelled most of them — log unofficially

parts.note: an event that is cancelled is off

indicators.note: most of means the word minus its last letter

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone scrapped nearly all the entries in a journal without authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts THEM to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark off the record is made unofficially, not for publication.
